solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Transport judge on yacht, first of all

indicators.note: first of all tells us to take the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: first letter of judge
first letter of on
first letter of yacht

explanation.surface: A judge is carried away aboard a yacht, as if on a pleasure cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like a verb about moving the judge, but it is the noun meaning rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in transports is to be overcome with delight, so transport here is a synonym for great happiness.

clue.text: Elephant: black thing that flies!

parts.note: Jumbo was a famous elephant, and the name is used for any elephant
jet is a deep glossy black, as in jet-black

explanation.surface: An exclamation imagining a flying elephant, Dumbo-style.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumbo jet is a large wide-bodied airliner, the Boeing 747 being the classic one.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger aircraft is plainly something that flies, a vague but fair description of an airliner.

clue.text: Complained peevishly, upsetting me, my dear!

indicators.note: upsetting suggests knocking things over, so the letters of the following words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that they were upset, addressing a companion fondly as 'my dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is to whine or complain loudly and persistently, so it matches grumbling in a peevish way.

clue.text: I'd turned back, seeing difference of opinion

indicators.note: turned back says the letters of I'd are to be read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the letters I and D, ignoring the apostrophe
seeing, as a noun, is the faculty of sight, or vision

explanation.surface: Someone turned round on seeing that people disagreed.
explanation.definitionFit: A division is a split or disagreement between groups, such as a rift in a party over policy.

clue.text: Metal leg, able to be pressed into place

definitions.text: able to be pressed into place

parts.note: iron is a metal
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A metal leg, perhaps a prosthesis, can be pushed into position.
explanation.walkthrough: ON for 'leg' comes from cricket, where the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron-on patch or label is fixed by pressing it with a hot iron, so it is applied by pressure.

clue.text: Some obtain an estimate that's most foolish

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dig at the idea that asking for a quote is the silliest thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, so its superlative describes whatever is the silliest of all.

clue.text: Keen on one set of books only, at first

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: at first asks for just the opening letter of the word only

parts.note: first letter of only

explanation.surface: A reader who is keen on just a single series of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is informal for being enthusiastic about it, as in being into jazz.

clue.text: Old imperial Roman, or Egyptian, gutted after revolution

indicators.note: after revolution means the letters, once turned round, are read in reverse order
gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters of Egyptian

parts.note: outer letters of Egyptian

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman or Egyptian ruler was disembowelled after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egyptian' looks like an alternative to Roman, but it is fodder; 'or' is fodder too, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a first-century emperor of Rome, so he is an old imperial Roman.

clue.text: Cosy in US, indulge every so often

indicators.note: every so often means only some letters are used, taking every other one

explanation.surface: Comfort in America lets you pamper yourself now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every so often' takes the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of US INDULGE; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug describes a warm, comfortable and sheltered place, the same feeling as cosy.

clue.text: Souvenir of yours truly, without article, meant nothing

parts.note: yours truly is a jocular way of saying me

indicators.note: without says a letter is taken out of the word meant

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A keepsake from you, without any items, meant nothing to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is an object kept as a reminder of a person or event, a keepsake.

clue.text: A large protective coat for church table

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
tar is spread as a protective coating on roads, roofs and boats

explanation.surface: A big protective covering is wanted for the table in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the raised table in a church at which communion is celebrated.

clue.text: Love song composed about very English kitchen accessories

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the others
composed suggests music being written, and here the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A love song is written about some very English kitchen items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges LOVE SONG; 'about' wraps those letters round VE, placed after the seventh letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oven gloves are padded mitts for handling hot dishes, an item found in any kitchen.

clue.text: Larks, in a whirl, land in Indian Ocean

indicators.note: a whirl spins things round, so the letters are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: Larks spinning in the air come down on an island in the Indian Ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' looks like part of the phrase 'in a whirl', but IN and A are anagram fodder alongside LARKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is an island nation south of India, a country in the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Regretful writer, one with temporary accommodation

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the Roman numeral I is one
a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: A rueful author camping out for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitent means feeling sorrow and remorse for wrongdoing, i.e. sorry.

clue.text: Editor's bringing people in for edits

indicators.note: bringing ... in says one group of letters is taken inside another
completes bringing ... in, putting the second piece inside the first

parts.note: ED is short for editor, and the 's adds an S
men are people

explanation.surface: An editor brings in staff to revise the text.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or improve a text, so it is a synonym for making edits.

clue.text: Old and dull doctor that is descending on Irish party

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first pieces come down and sit on top of what follows

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A doctor, i.e. a boring old one, swoops on a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP, the Democratic Unionist Party, is a Northern Irish political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried-up describes someone past their prime and lacking vitality, so elderly and boring.

clue.text: Celebrity vet has removed tail fast

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

indicators.note: removing the tail means the final letter of vet is cut off

explanation.surface: A famous animal doctor has docked a tail very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like an adverb meaning quickly, but it is the verb for going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to go without food, which is what fasting means.

clue.text: Pact, at heart, what's needed for binding agreement

indicators.note: at heart asks for the central letters of the word pact

parts.note: middle letters of Pact
cord is string used to tie things up

explanation.surface: The essence of a treaty is what makes an agreement binding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding agreement' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'agreement'.
explanation.definitionFit: An accord is a formal agreement or treaty, or a state of harmony between parties.

clue.text: Choose a bloomer, reportedly for hot sauce

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are heard rather than read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to choose is to pick, and a lily is a flower, a bloomer

explanation.surface: Pick out a flower to go with a spicy condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' could be a blunder or a loaf of bread, but here it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Piccalilli is a bright yellow mustard-and-vegetable pickle relish with a spicy kick.

clue.text: Send up and look at daily paper

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, as in lo and behold
the FT, the Financial Times, is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Mock something, then read the morning paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send up' suggests mockery, but it means hitting a ball high; the FT is the Financial Times, a British daily.
explanation.definitionFit: To loft a ball is to hit or kick it high into the air, sending it upwards.

clue.text: A girl is too short, sad to say

indicators.note: too short means the word is cut back, losing its final letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl is lamentably small in stature.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection of regret, used to introduce unfortunate news.

clue.text: Thirty seconds, perhaps, to put on one's skirt

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: thirty seconds is half a minute, so half of MINUTE is taken
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone takes just half a minute to get dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Thirty seconds is half a minute, so the first half of MINUTE is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a very short skirt, short for miniskirt.

clue.text: One embraced by fat Scottish landowner

indicators.note: embraced by means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: lard is pig fat
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone is hugged by a stout laird.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is the owner of a landed estate in Scotland.

clue.text: Crime relating to fight with sword

parts.note: of can mean concerning, relating to
to fence is to fight with swords as a sport

explanation.surface: An offence involving a fight with a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of law, an illegal act.

clue.text: Five hundred in unusual Spanish football gear

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
unusual means the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Five hundred items of strange Spanish football kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges SPANISH; 'in' puts D after the fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shin pads are protective guards worn on the lower legs by footballers.

clue.text: Insect found in Quantocks

indicators.note: found in tells us the answer sits inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A bug discovered in the Quantocks, hills in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An ant is a small social insect living in colonies.
